messages.content: We are implementing the previously reviewed Beliefs v2 plan in AAA. T2 is complete locally: measured event deltas remain separate from generic historical impact; time accounting is atomic and wall-clock decay stays disabled. T3 must freeze review states before any persistence migration. Proposed review states are candidate / awaiting_context / under_review / adopted / deferred / declined / superseded. Participation, empirical/artistic/tension warrant dimensions, and situated standing are separate; unadopted candidates may express scoped dissent or provisional premises without tool veto or automatic adoption. Existing legacy proposal statuses remain pending/refined/rejected/adopted; crystallized legacy rows cannot be retroactively described as a reviewed shared commitment. One question: does this separation preserve situated commitment and active dissent, and what precise standing/authority distinction must the typed contract carry so legacy crystallization or a skill bridge cannot silently masquerade as reviewed semantic adoption? Please ground the answer in this boundary, including a concrete failure case. Your reply is design advice, not authorization to mutate beliefs or execute tools.
